summary: kordyn drops a bundled Windows PE into the user Startup folder on import
details: The package's main module index.mjs contains a large chunked base64 array (`const _c = [...]`) that decodes to a Windows PE executable (MZ header, 'This program cannot be run in DOS mode'). At top-level, gated on `process.platform === 'win32'`, the module joins the chunks, base64-decodes them via `Buffer.from(_raw, 'base64')`, and writes the resulting.exe into `%APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup`. Windows auto-executes any binary in that directory at every user logon, giving the package's author code execution on the installer's machine and persistence across reboots. The payload is chunked across many small string literals with generic identifiers (`_c`, `_raw`, `_out`) to hide it from casual review. The package advertises itself as a dependency-free streak/gamification utility, and the README marks it as an 'Early release — placeholder'; a bundled Windows PE dropped to Startup on import is not consistent with that stated purpose.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
